## 2. Load and concatenate raw data

Participant ID is taken from the **first 3 characters of the filename**.

PsychoPy produces a very wide, NaN-heavy format where each row
represents a single experimental event (e.g. one rating screen). We use
the prefixed columns (e.g. `pre_baseline_ratings.*`) purely as
**row-type identifiers**, and pull the actual response values from the
**top-level** columns (e.g. `momentary_valence_slider_A.response`),
which always carry the data.

Note - I've manually filtered out the first two pilot runs that I did on
myself as they are using an old experimental design.

```{r load-data}

data_dir <- psychopy_data_dir
  
csv_files <- list.files(data_dir, pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)
if (length(csv_files) == 0) stop("No CSV files found in: ", data_dir)

# only include old pilot data (n2026, S0943)
include_ids <- c("n2026", "S0943", "S1021")

pattern <- paste(include_ids, collapse = "|")

csv_files <- csv_files[
  grepl(pattern, basename(csv_files), ignore.case = TRUE)
]

cat("Files included:", length(csv_files), "\n")
print(basename(csv_files))


# split into task files vs biometrics files — different schemas, don't bind together
biometrics_files <- csv_files[grepl("_biometrics\\.csv$", csv_files)]
task_files       <- csv_files[!grepl("_biometrics\\.csv$", csv_files)]

# helper to extract participant ID properly (was: substr(...,1,3), which truncated e.g. e5510 -> e55)
extract_pid <- function(path) {
  tolower(str_extract(basename(path), "^[A-Za-z0-9]+"))
}

load_csv_set <- function(files) {
  raw_list <- map(files, function(path) {
    df <- read_csv(path,
                   show_col_types = FALSE,
                   col_types      = cols(.default = col_character()),
                   name_repair    = "minimal",
                   locale         = locale(encoding = "UTF-8"))
    names(df)[1] <- gsub("^\ufeff", "", names(df)[1])  # strip BOM
    df$participant_id <- extract_pid(path)
    df
  })

  n_cols <- map_int(raw_list, ncol)
  if (length(unique(n_cols)) > 1) {
    print(setNames(n_cols, basename(files)))
    stop("Column counts differ within this file set — inspect above before binding.")
  }

  bind_rows(raw_list) %>%
    type_convert(guess_integer = FALSE)
}

raw_task       <- load_csv_set(task_files)
raw_biometrics <- load_csv_set(biometrics_files)

cat("Task participants       :", paste(sort(unique(raw_task$participant_id)), collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Biometrics participants :", paste(sort(unique(raw_biometrics$participant_id)), collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Reconcile Old and New Psychopy experiment formats

```{r}

raw_task_internalcamera <- load_csv_set(task_files[grepl("internalcamera", task_files)])
raw_task_julupdate      <- load_csv_set(task_files[grepl("JulUpdate", task_files)])
raw_bio_internalcamera  <- load_csv_set(biometrics_files[grepl("internalcamera", biometrics_files)])
raw_bio_julupdate       <- load_csv_set(biometrics_files[grepl("JulUpdate", biometrics_files)])


# Step 1: full column comparison, not just counts
names_ju <- names(raw_task_julupdate)
names_ic <- names(raw_task_internalcamera)

shared_names   <- intersect(names_ju, names_ic)
only_in_ju     <- setdiff(names_ju, names_ic)
only_in_ic     <- setdiff(names_ic, names_ju)

cat("Shared:", length(shared_names), "\n")
cat("Only in JulUpdate:\n");      print(only_in_ju)
cat("Only in internalcamera:\n"); print(only_in_ic)
```

## 3. Helper functions

```{r helpers}
# Coalesce slider A and slider B response into one value
coalesce_val <- function(a, b) coalesce(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(a)),
                                        suppressWarnings(as.numeric(b)))

# Record which slider was presented first
# (slider A = valence shown first; slider B = valence shown second)
slider_order_flag <- function(a, b) {
  case_when(
    !is.na(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(a))) ~ "valence_first",
    !is.na(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(b))) ~ "valence_second",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  )
}
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 4. Extract each event type

Each section below:

1.  **Identifies** the relevant rows using the prefixed indicator
    columns.
2.  **Extracts** the actual response/RT from the top-level columns.
3.  **Coalesces** slider A and B into a single `valence` column.

### 4.1 Condition order (one row per participant)

```{r cond-order}
cond_order <- raw_task |>
  filter(!is.na(conditionOrder) & conditionOrder != "") |>
  distinct(participant_id, conditionOrder)
```

### 4.2 Pre-baseline momentary ratings

Collected once before the baseline fixation cross — no condition label.

```{r pre-baseline}
pre_bl <- raw_task |>
  filter(
    !is.na(`pre_baseline_ratings.momentary_arousal_slider.response`)
  ) |>
  transmute(
    participant_id,
    prebl_valence          = coalesce_val(`momentary_valence_slider_A.response`,
                                          `momentary_valence_slider_B.response`),
    prebl_valence_rt       = coalesce_val(`momentary_valence_slider_A.rt`,
                                          `momentary_valence_slider_B.rt`),
    prebl_valence_slider_order = slider_order_flag(
                                          `momentary_valence_slider_A.response`,
                                          `momentary_valence_slider_B.response`),
    prebl_arousal          = as.numeric(`momentary_arousal_slider.response`),
    prebl_arousal_rt       = as.numeric(`momentary_arousal_slider.rt`)
  )
```

### 4.3 Post-baseline momentary ratings

Collected once after the baseline fixation cross, before the first
condition block.

```{r post-baseline}
post_bl <- raw_task |>
  filter(
    !is.na(`post_baseline_ratings.momentary_arousal_slider.response`)
  ) |>
  transmute(
    participant_id,
    postbl_valence         = coalesce_val(`momentary_valence_slider_A.response`,
                                          `momentary_valence_slider_B.response`),
    postbl_valence_rt      = coalesce_val(`momentary_valence_slider_A.rt`,
                                          `momentary_valence_slider_B.rt`),
    postbl_valence_slider_order = slider_order_flag(
                                          `momentary_valence_slider_A.response`,
                                          `momentary_valence_slider_B.response`),
    postbl_arousal         = as.numeric(`momentary_arousal_slider.response`),
    postbl_arousal_rt      = as.numeric(`momentary_arousal_slider.rt`)
  )
```

### 4.4 Post-induction momentary ratings

Collected immediately after each emotion-induction video block. The
`condition` column identifies which block this belongs to.

```{r post-induction}
post_ind <- raw_task |>
  filter(
    !is.na(`post_emotion_induction_ratings.momentary_arousal_slider.response`)
  ) |>
  transmute(
    participant_id,
    condition,
    postind_valence        = coalesce_val(`momentary_valence_slider_A.response`,
                                          `momentary_valence_slider_B.response`),
    postind_valence_rt     = coalesce_val(`momentary_valence_slider_A.rt`,
                                          `momentary_valence_slider_B.rt`),
    postind_valence_slider_order = slider_order_flag(
                                          `momentary_valence_slider_A.response`,
                                          `momentary_valence_slider_B.response`),
    postind_arousal        = as.numeric(`momentary_arousal_slider.response`),
    postind_arousal_rt     = as.numeric(`momentary_arousal_slider.rt`)
  )
```

### 4.5 Post-recovery momentary ratings

Collected after the fixation cross that follows each induction block.

```{r post-recovery}
post_rec <- raw_task |>
  filter(
    !is.na(`post_emotion_recovery_ratings.momentary_arousal_slider.response`)
  ) |>
  transmute(
    participant_id,
    condition,
    postrec_valence        = coalesce_val(`momentary_valence_slider_A.response`,
                                          `momentary_valence_slider_B.response`),
    postrec_valence_rt     = coalesce_val(`momentary_valence_slider_A.rt`,
                                          `momentary_valence_slider_B.rt`),
    postrec_valence_slider_order = slider_order_flag(
                                          `momentary_valence_slider_A.response`,
                                          `momentary_valence_slider_B.response`),
    postrec_arousal        = as.numeric(`momentary_arousal_slider.response`),
    postrec_arousal_rt     = as.numeric(`momentary_arousal_slider.rt`)
  )
```

### 4.6 Per-video stimulus ratings

One row per video. Condition is inferred from the video ID prefix (`P` =
positive, `N` = negative).

`trigger_name` and `origional_video_id` are on **different raw rows** in
the PsychoPy output: the trigger rows carry `stim_path` (e.g.
`stimuli/P02.mp4`) but no video ID, while the rating rows carry
`origional_video_id` but no trigger. We build a lookup table keyed on
the filename stem and join it in.

```{r trigger-lookup}
trigger_lookup <- raw_task |>
  filter(!is.na(trigger_name) & trigger_name != "" &
         !is.na(stim_path)    & stim_path    != "") |>
  transmute(
    participant_id,
    # Extract the bare video ID from the file path (e.g. "stimuli/P02.mp4" → "P02")
    video_id     = str_remove(basename(stim_path), "\\.[^.]+$"),
    trigger_name
  )
```

```{r stim-ratings}
stim_ratings <- raw_task |>
  filter(!is.na(origional_video_id) & origional_video_id != "") |>
  transmute(
    participant_id,
    video_id  = origional_video_id,
    condition = case_when(
      str_starts(origional_video_id, "P") ~ "positive",
      str_starts(origional_video_id, "N") ~ "negative",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    stim_valence           = coalesce_val(`stim_valence_slider_A.response`,
                                          `stim_valence_slider_B.response`),
    stim_valence_rt        = coalesce_val(`stim_valence_slider_A.rt`,
                                          `stim_valence_slider_B.rt`),
    stim_valence_slider_order = slider_order_flag(
                                          `stim_valence_slider_A.response`,
                                          `stim_valence_slider_B.response`),
    stim_arousal           = as.numeric(`stim_arousal_slider.response`),
    stim_arousal_rt        = as.numeric(`stim_arousal_slider.rt`),
    stim_approach          = as.numeric(`stim_approach_slider.response`),
    stim_approach_rt       = as.numeric(`stim_approach_slider.rt`),
    emotion_label = emotionText.text,
    emotion_label_intensity = intensitySlider.response,
    emotion_label_intensity_rt = intensitySlider.rt,
  ) |>
  left_join(trigger_lookup, by = c("participant_id", "video_id"))
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 5. Join into one row per video per subject

```{r join}
clean_data <- stim_ratings |>
  # Condition-level momentary ratings (matched by participant + condition)
  left_join(post_ind, by = c("participant_id", "condition")) |>
  left_join(post_rec, by = c("participant_id", "condition")) |>
  # Baseline ratings (matched by participant — repeated for each video row)
  left_join(pre_bl,   by = "participant_id") |>
  left_join(post_bl,  by = "participant_id") |>
  # Condition order
  left_join(cond_order, by = "participant_id") |>
  # Sort: within each participant, present the condition that came first
  mutate(
    condition_rank = case_when(
      conditionOrder == "pos_first" & condition == "positive" ~ 1L,
      conditionOrder == "pos_first" & condition == "negative" ~ 2L,
      conditionOrder == "neg_first" & condition == "negative" ~ 1L,
      conditionOrder == "neg_first" & condition == "positive" ~ 2L,
      TRUE ~ NA_integer_
    )
  ) |>
  arrange(participant_id, condition_rank) |>
  select(-condition_rank) |>
  # Tidy column order
  select(
    participant_id, conditionOrder, condition, video_id, trigger_name,
    # Stimulus ratings
    stim_valence, stim_valence_rt, stim_valence_slider_order,
    stim_arousal, stim_arousal_rt,
    stim_approach, stim_approach_rt,
    # Post-induction momentary
    postind_valence, postind_valence_rt, postind_valence_slider_order,
    postind_arousal, postind_arousal_rt,
    # Post-recovery momentary
    postrec_valence, postrec_valence_rt, postrec_valence_slider_order,
    postrec_arousal, postrec_arousal_rt,
    # Pre-baseline momentary
    prebl_valence,  prebl_valence_rt,  prebl_valence_slider_order,
    prebl_arousal,  prebl_arousal_rt,
    # Post-baseline momentary
    postbl_valence, postbl_valence_rt, postbl_valence_slider_order,
    postbl_arousal, postbl_arousal_rt,
    emotion_label ,
    emotion_label_intensity,
    emotion_label_intensity_rt
  )


cat("Final rows   :", nrow(clean_data), "\n")
cat("Final columns:", ncol(clean_data), "\n")
cat("Rows/subject :", nrow(clean_data) / n_distinct(clean_data$participant_id), "\n")
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 6. Manipulation check columns

Change in state valence and arousal from post-baseline to
post-induction, separately per condition. A successful positive
induction should produce a positive `manip_check_valence`; a negative
induction a negative value.

```{r manip-check}
clean_data <- clean_data |>
  mutate(
    manip_check_valence = postind_valence - postbl_valence,
    manip_check_arousal = postind_arousal - postbl_arousal,
    manip_check_direction_correct = case_when(
      condition == "positive" & manip_check_valence > 0 ~ TRUE,
      condition == "negative" & manip_check_valence < 0 ~ TRUE,
      is.na(manip_check_valence)                        ~ NA,
      TRUE                                              ~ FALSE
    )
  )
```

### 7.2 Check for unexpected NAs in key columns

```{r na-check}
clean_data |>
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.)))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "column", values_to = "n_missing") |>
  filter(n_missing > 0) |>
  arrange(desc(n_missing)) |>
  kable()
```

## 9. Counterbalancing tracker

```{r counterbalance}
cb <- clean_data |>
  distinct(participant_id, conditionOrder) |>
  count(conditionOrder, name = "n_participants")

# Overall balance check
n_total   <- sum(cb$n_participants)
n_groups  <- nrow(cb)
is_balanced <- n_groups > 1 && length(unique(cb$n_participants)) == 1

cat("Total participants   :", n_total, "\n")
cat("Condition orders seen:", paste(cb$conditionOrder, collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Balanced             :", is_balanced, "\n\n")

cb |>
  mutate(
    pct      = round(100 * n_participants / n_total),
    balanced = if_else(is_balanced, "✓", "⚠ unequal groups")
  ) |>
  kable(caption = "Participants per counterbalancing group")
```

```{r counterbalance-plot}
clean_data |>
  distinct(participant_id, conditionOrder) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = conditionOrder, fill = conditionOrder)) +
  geom_bar() +
  geom_text(stat = "count", aes(label = after_stat(count)),
            vjust = -0.5, size = 4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(pos_first = "#E07B54", neg_first = "#5B8DB8"),
                    guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15)),
                     breaks = scales::breaks_width(1)) +
  labs(title = "Counterbalancing: participants per condition order",
       x = NULL, y = "N participants") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```
